description: REQ-105/REQ-305 repurpose `~/anicca/skills/economy/ubi/colony-wallets.json` from its CURRENT, actually-used role ('addresses proven to be real colony members' -- ubi.js's own JSDoc for the exact array this file is fed into, gating WHO may passively RECEIVE a mutual-aid gift) into a materially different, much higher-stakes role: THE registry REQ-101 aggregates SURPLUS from to decide whether the colony may fund a brand-new autonomous spawn. Neither REQ-105 nor its Purity Boundary/PROP-105 entries ever notice that the file's CURRENT 2nd entry, `0x904B50d2e214Da947d83D6a2D32c4E3Ffc17Eb74`, is claude-p's OWN wallet -- this project's own on-disk canonical wallet ledger (`docs/WALLETS.md` line 54: "claude-p is the exception: its real funds sit in the Polymarket deposit wallet 0x904B50d2e214Da947d83D6a2D32c4E3Ffc17Eb74") confirms this is the human-funded (Anthropic-subscription-fueled) entity that behavioral-spec.md's own Scope section says SPEC.md §0's HARD invariant must permanently keep OUT of colony surplus ("claude-p + 全 human-funded AI は経済圏の永久非構成員"). REQ-105's acceptance criteria (behavioral-spec.md) and PROP-105c (verification-architecture.md line 91) both assert migration 'preserves each entry's existing wallet address value(s) unchanged' and 'preserves each one's known-good isSelfFunded() verdict (no silent reclassification)' -- but the CURRENT file (a bare array of 3 address strings, colony-wallets.json:1-5) carries ZERO fuel/humanDependencies metadata, so there IS no pre-existing 'known-good isSelfFunded() verdict' computable from today's data at all (isSelfFunded() requires an object with wallet/fuel/humanDependencies; a bare string was never run through it). PROP-105c's own proof method ('compare against today's known-good identities') is therefore incoherent as written: the only way an implementer can correctly classify entry #2 as isSelfFunded()===false is by importing OUT-OF-BAND knowledge (which wallet belongs to which entity) that this spec never states, cites, or tests. If an implementer instead infers fuel.provider generically (e.g. copies whichever provider value the sibling entries get, or leaves it blank and a later code path defaults it), claude-p's own wallet balance could silently enter REQ-101's colony-surplus aggregate that gates REQ-102's spawn-funding decision -- the exact failure mode this feature's own Scope section calls out as the one thing this spec must prevent. This is a live, on-disk, concrete violation risk in the very file the feature's central treasury gate reads from, not a hypothetical.

evidence.snippet: THE SYSTEM SHALL read that list from a single, versioned JSON registry file (`~/anicca/skills/economy/ubi/colony-wallets.json`), extended from its CURRENT flat bare-address-array shape (`["0x...", "0x...", "8Fpqd..."]`) into an array of citizen-record objects, each carrying EXACTLY the fields isSelfFunded()/selfFundedReasons() ... already require

additionalEvidence.note: canonical, on-disk confirmation that 0x904B50d2e214Da947d83D6a2D32c4E3Ffc17Eb74 is claude-p's own (human-funded) real funding wallet, the 'exception' explicitly called out as needing special handling elsewhere in this project's own bookkeeping

distributeAI's own JSDoc: 'registrySignedWallets - addresses proven to be real colony members (not a bare list)' -- confirms colony-wallets.json's CURRENT semantic role is recipient-eligibility for mutual aid, a different purpose than the surplus-aggregation registry REQ-105 repurposes it into
PROP-105c's proof method ('compare against today's known-good identities') presupposes a ground truth that cannot be derived from the current bare-address file's data model alone
the Scope section's own statement of the HARD invariant this exact gap threatens
